input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting it fixed. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I need my mobile internet to work perfectly. Can you help me with this?
My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough—I don’t remember my customer ID. What should I do next?
Yes, it’s the same number—555-123-2002. That’s the only phone I use. What should I do now?

Okay, looking at the top of my phone, I see just one bar for signal strength, and it says 2G. There’s a little mobile data icon, and my battery is at 80%. I don’t see an airplane icon anywhere. 

Is that helpful? What should I do next?

Alright, I changed the setting to prefer 4G/5G, and now the top of my screen shows four bars for signal strength and says 5G. The mobile data icon is still there, and my battery is still at 80%.

What should I do next? Will this make my internet excellent now?

Oh, I tried to do a speed test like you suggested, but it says there’s no connection. I thought it would work since it shows 5G and full bars now. What should I do? Is there something else I need to try?
I checked, and it says my SIM card is active and working. What should I do next? I’m still not getting any internet, even though it shows 5G and full bars.

I found something called “internet” listed as the APN name, and there’s a web address for picture messages. I don’t see any error messages or anything that looks strange, but I’m not really sure what I’m looking at.

Should I still reset the APN settings, or is there something else I should try? I just want to make sure I don’t mess anything up.

I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. Now, you mentioned I should restart my phone—will that erase any of my photos or anything important? I get a bit nervous about restarting things. Can you reassure me that it’s safe before I do it?

Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t get the internet to work. I tried running a speed test again, and it still says there’s no connection. What should I do now? I really need excellent internet speed on my phone.

I removed and reinserted the SIM card like you suggested, but I’m still not getting any internet. The speed test still says there’s no connection, even though it shows 5G and full bars at the top. 

Is there anything else I can try? I really need excellent internet speed—nothing less will do.

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting it fixed. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I need my mobile internet to work perfectly. Can you help me with this?

I can help you with your mobile data issues. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account so I can check your line and data status. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID (if you know it)?

Once I have this information, I’ll guide you step-by-step to resolve your mobile data problem.
My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough—I don’t remember my customer ID. What should I do next?

Thank you for providing your information, John. I’ve found your account. To help fix your mobile data issue, I’ll need to check a few things about your line and data usage.

Could you please confirm which phone number (or line) you are having trouble with, especially if you have more than one line on your account? Is it the same number you provided (555-123-2002), or a different one? 

Once you confirm, I’ll guide you through the next steps to diagnose and resolve your mobile data problem.
Yes, it’s the same number—555-123-2002. That’s the only phone I use. What should I do now?

Thank you for confirming. To diagnose your mobile data issue, I’ll guide you through a few simple checks on your phone. This will help us find out why your data is slow or not working.

First, please check your phone’s status bar (the area at the top of your screen) and let me know:
- Do you see any airplane icon (✈️)?
- What is the signal strength (bars or dots)?
- Do you see a network type indicator (like 5G, 4G, LTE, etc.)?
- Is there a mobile data icon (like 📱 or similar)?

If you’re not sure how to check, let me know and I can guide you step-by-step.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Okay, looking at the top of my phone, I see just one bar for signal strength, and it says 2G. There’s a little mobile data icon, and my battery is at 80%. I don’t see an airplane icon anywhere. 

Is that helpful? What should I do next?

Thank you for checking! That information is very helpful. Since your phone is showing only one bar of signal strength and is connected to a 2G network, this is likely the main reason your mobile data is slow or not working well. 2G networks are very slow and not suitable for modern internet use.

Let’s try to improve your connection by switching your phone’s network mode to prefer 4G or 5G (if available). Please follow these steps on your phone:
1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Find the section called “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
3. Look for an option called “Preferred network type” or “Network mode.”
4. Change it to “4G/5G preferred” or “LTE/5G preferred” (if available).

After you make this change, please check your status bar again and let me know:
- If the network type changes from 2G to 4G, LTE, or 5G.
- If your signal strength improves.

If you need step-by-step instructions for your specific phone model, let me know!

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Alright, I changed the setting to prefer 4G/5G, and now the top of my screen shows four bars for signal strength and says 5G. The mobile data icon is still there, and my battery is still at 80%.

What should I do next? Will this make my internet excellent now?

That’s great progress! Now that your phone is showing four bars and is connected to 5G, your mobile data should be much faster and more reliable.

To confirm everything is working as expected, please try using your mobile internet (for example, open a website or app that needs internet). If you want to be sure about your connection speed, you can also run a speed test using your phone.

Let me know:
- Is your internet working well now?
- Do you notice a big improvement in speed?
- Would you like instructions on how to run a speed test on your phone?

If you still experience any issues, I can guide you through more troubleshooting steps.
Speed test failed: No Connection.

Oh, I tried to do a speed test like you suggested, but it says there’s no connection. I thought it would work since it shows 5G and full bars now. What should I do? Is there something else I need to try?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your phone now shows 5G and full bars but still says there’s no connection when running a speed test, there may be an issue with your mobile data settings or SIM card.

Let’s try the following steps to diagnose the problem:

1. Please check if your SIM card is active and working correctly. On your phone, look for an option called “SIM status” or “SIM card status” in your settings (usually under “About phone” or “Network & Internet”).
2. Let me know what it says about your SIM card (for example: Active, Missing, or Locked).

If you’re not sure how to find this, let me know your phone model and I can guide you step-by-step. Once you provide this information, I’ll help you with the next steps.
Your SIM card is active and working.
I checked, and it says my SIM card is active and working. What should I do next? I’m still not getting any internet, even though it shows 5G and full bars.

Thank you for checking your SIM card status. Since your SIM is active, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent your phone from accessing mobile data, even if you have a strong signal.

Please look for “APN settings” or “Access Point Names” in your phone’s settings (usually under “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network”). Check if there is an APN listed, and if so, let me know if anything looks unusual or if there’s an error message.

If you’re unsure, I recommend resetting your APN settings to default. Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I found something called “internet” listed as the APN name, and there’s a web address for picture messages. I don’t see any error messages or anything that looks strange, but I’m not really sure what I’m looking at.

Should I still reset the APN settings, or is there something else I should try? I just want to make sure I don’t mess anything up.

Thank you for checking your APN settings. Even if nothing looks obviously wrong, sometimes resetting the APN settings can resolve hidden issues and won’t harm your phone. It will simply restore the correct settings for your carrier.

Here’s what I recommend:
- Please reset your APN settings to default.
- After resetting, restart (reboot) your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your phone? If so, please let me know your phone’s make and model (for example, Samsung Galaxy S21, iPhone 13, etc.), and I’ll guide you through the process.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. Now, you mentioned I should restart my phone—will that erase any of my photos or anything important? I get a bit nervous about restarting things. Can you reassure me that it’s safe before I do it?

Restarting (rebooting) your phone is completely safe and will not erase any of your photos, messages, apps, or other important information. It simply turns your phone off and back on again, which helps apply the new settings and can fix temporary issues.

You can safely restart your phone now. Once it turns back on, please check if your mobile data is working. If you still have issues, let me know and I’ll help you with the next steps.
